# KS-1081 R16B-CANONENV - re-brief at develop 8c2f7b3fd of READY_KS-1081_ornith35b-q4_BASHPATCH-NEWTEST-PASS-7of7_2026-09-16.diff.md (written 2026-09-22 10:26:40 AEST by Wednesday's feed9 drafter under the FEED 8 ruling; the product hunk and the new suite are the old READY's PASS 7/7 output re-anchored at the tip (KS-1081: one hunk corrected to the old brief's intent - see the drafter's note), every '+' line and every suite line made ASCII: the cell glyph is the word RED, em-dashes are hyphens; every context and '-' line asserted byte-exact at the tip at the line numbers below)

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_canonical_template.test.sh`
Tip: 8c2f7b3fd4fde915b2a24542bc32259b24e092a0
Runner: bash (the shell suite runner - `bash <file>` under /bin/bash 3.2; the checker runs the suite alone at the tip, then again after the script hunk)

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
`Blockchain/Dev/` carries **two tracked env templates** — `env.example` (444 lines, 102 distinct
variables) and `.env.example` (327 lines, 65 variables) — and the two consumers read different ones.
`scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:26` sets `ENV_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"`, while the documentation
documents the other file: `Blockchain/Dev/README.md:25` and `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:26` both
say `cp env.example .env`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:130` and `docs/DEVELOPER-GUIDE.md:53` say the same, and
`docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md:13-15` names `env.example` as *the* core infrastructure template. So a
developer who follows the docs and a developer who runs the script get environments that differ by
**64 variables** (measured: the generated `.env` from the tip is missing 64 of the 102 that
`env.example` declares, including `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS`, every `AUTH0_*`, every `AZURE_AD_*`, every
`STRIPE_*`, `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` and `VITE_ENABLE_DEMO`). **Kam ruled it: "env.example (the larger,
the one CLAUDE.md documents) is canonical."** This task points the script at the canonical template,
names it in the operator-visible message, and keeps the legacy name alive only as a fallback for a
tree that carries no `env.example` — because two existing harnesses build exactly such a tree
(`scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh:91` and
`scripts/verify-slot-credential-isolation.sh:59` each write only `.env.example` into a scratch clone
and then run this script), and breaking them is not part of the ruling. NOT in this task: editing
either template file, deleting `.env.example`, or reconciling the 30 variables that `.env.example`
declares and `env.example` does not — that is the separate reconciliation half of the KS-1077 shape.
## Drafter's note (feed9, read before the hunk)
CORRECTION vs the old READY (feed9 drafter): the old READY's hunk 2 removed `  exit 1` and kept the old `print_error ".env.example not found at: ..."` line - the reverse of what the old brief asked (KS-1081.md: replace the message line, keep `exit 1`), and a real defect (a missing template would no longer stop the script by that guard). Hunk 2 below is the BRIEF's shape: the `-` line is the old `print_error` message, the `+` line is the new message, `  exit 1` stays as context. Nothing else differs from the old READY. The suite has no cell on the missing-template path, so B4/B5 read the same lines either way. Scope note from the old READY: the NAMED legacy fallback (`ENV_EXAMPLE_LEGACY`) is deliberate and must stay until the two templates are reconciled.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TEST: bootstrap-env.sh copies the CANONICAL template env.example (KS-1081)
# =============================================================================
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_canonical_template.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
DEV_DIR="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
BOOTSTRAP="${BOOTSTRAP_SH:-$HERE/../bootstrap-env.sh}"
ENV_SH="$HERE/../stack_env.sh"
CANONICAL="$DEV_DIR/env.example"
LEGACY="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"
[[ -f "$BOOTSTRAP" ]] || { echo "FATAL: bootstrap-env.sh not found at $BOOTSTRAP" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$ENV_SH" ]]    || { echo "FATAL: stack_env.sh not found at $ENV_SH" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$CANONICAL" ]] || { echo "FATAL: canonical template not found at $CANONICAL" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$LEGACY" ]]    || { echo "FATAL: legacy template not found at $LEGACY" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: openssl required (bootstrap-env.sh needs it)" >&2; exit 2; }
PASS=0
FAIL=0

var_names() { grep -E '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=' "$1" | cut -d= -f1 | sort -u; }
GENERATED='^(POSTGRES_PASSWORD|DATABASE_URL|REDIS_PASSWORD|REDIS_URL|PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY|PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION|PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY|DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED|DEMO_SERVICE_KEY|JWT_PRIVATE_KEY|JWT_PUBLIC_KEY|JWT_KEY_ID)$'
CANON_ONLY="$(comm -23 <(var_names "$CANONICAL") <(var_names "$LEGACY") | grep -vE "$GENERATED" | head -n1)"
[[ -n "$CANON_ONLY" ]] || { echo "FATAL: the two templates no longer differ outside the script-generated keys - premise of this suite changed" >&2; exit 2; }

SCRATCH_ROOT="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1081.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$SCRATCH_ROOT"' EXIT
BOTH="$SCRATCH_ROOT/both/Blockchain/Dev"
mkdir -p "$BOTH/scripts"
cp "$BOOTSTRAP" "$BOTH/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh"
cp "$ENV_SH" "$BOTH/scripts/stack_env.sh"
cp "$CANONICAL" "$BOTH/env.example"
cp "$LEGACY" "$BOTH/.env.example"
env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT -u REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" bash "$BOTH/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh" >"$BOTH/bootstrap.log" 2>&1
BOTH_RC=$?

ONLY_LEGACY="$SCRATCH_ROOT/legacyonly/Blockchain/Dev"
mkdir -p "$ONLY_LEGACY/scripts"
cp "$BOOTSTRAP" "$ONLY_LEGACY/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh"
cp "$ENV_SH" "$ONLY_LEGACY/scripts/stack_env.sh"
cp "$LEGACY" "$ONLY_LEGACY/.env.example"
env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u STACK_SLOT -u POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT -u REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" bash "$ONLY_LEGACY/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh" >"$ONLY_LEGACY/bootstrap.log" 2>&1
LEGACY_RC=$?

MISSING_N="$(comm -23 <(var_names "$CANONICAL") <(var_names "$BOTH/.env") | grep -c .)"
MISSING="$(comm -23 <(var_names "$CANONICAL") <(var_names "$BOTH/.env") | head -n 6 | xargs)"
DB_PORT="$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' "$BOTH/.env" | head -n1 | sed -E 's#^.*@localhost:##; s#/.*$##')"

if [[ "$MISSING_N" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "PASS: every variable in env.example reached the generated .env"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: the generated .env is missing $MISSING_N variables that env.example declares (first 6: $MISSING)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

if grep -qE "^${CANON_ONLY}=" "$BOTH/.env"; then
  echo "PASS: the canonical-only variable $CANON_ONLY is in the generated .env"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: $CANON_ONLY is declared in env.example and absent from the generated .env - .env.example was copied"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

if grep -qF 'Created .env from env.example' "$BOTH/bootstrap.log"; then
  echo "PASS: the script reports the canonical template by name"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: the bootstrap log does not say 'Created .env from env.example'"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

if grep -qF '$DEV_DIR/env.example' "$BOOTSTRAP"; then
  echo "PASS: the script resolves the canonical template path under DEV_DIR"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: $BOOTSTRAP never names the canonical env.example path under DEV_DIR"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

if [[ "$BOTH_RC" -eq 0 && "$DB_PORT" == "6432" ]]; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL bootstrap exits 0 and DATABASE_URL still carries the slot-1 port 6432"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL bootstrap rc=$BOTH_RC, DATABASE_URL port '$DB_PORT' (want rc 0 and 6432)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

if [[ "$LEGACY_RC" -eq 0 && -f "$ONLY_LEGACY/.env" ]]; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL a tree carrying only .env.example still bootstraps (the fallback)"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else

fi

echo ""
echo "bootstrap_env_canonical_template: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"

files.Blockchain/Dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:
#!/bin/bash

# =============================================================================
# SECUURA LOCAL ENV BOOTSTRAP
# =============================================================================
# Creates Blockchain/Dev/.env and Blockchain/Dev/.env.local from their example
# files (if missing) and generates 32-byte hex keys for any PII secrets that
# are still blank.
#
# Idempotent — safe to re-run. Will not overwrite a non-empty existing value.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/bootstrap-env.sh
#
# After running this once, `docker compose up` should work without manual edits.
# =============================================================================

set -e

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Locate paths relative to this script (so it works from any cwd)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
DEV_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$DEV_DIR/.env"
ENV_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"
ENV_LOCAL_FILE="$DEV_DIR/.env.local"
ENV_LOCAL_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.local.example"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colours / helpers (matching scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh style)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m'

print_header()  { echo -e "\n${BLUE}==============================================================================${NC}"; echo -e "${BLUE}$1${NC}"; echo -e "${BLUE}==============================================================================${NC}\n"; }
print_success() { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
print_warning() { echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ $1${NC}"; }
print_error()   { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}"; }
print_info()    { echo -e "${BLUE}ℹ $1${NC}"; }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-flight
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
print_header "SECUURA ENV BOOTSTRAP"

if ! command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_error "openssl is required to generate keys but was not found in PATH."
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ENV_EXAMPLE" ]]; then
  print_error ".env.example not found at: $ENV_EXAMPLE"
  exit 1
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: copy .env from example if missing
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  print_info ".env already exists — leaving it untouched"
else
  cp "$ENV_EXAMPLE" "$ENV_FILE"
  print_success "Created .env from .env.example"
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: copy .env.local from example if missing (optional — only if example exists)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -f "$ENV_LOCAL_EXAMPLE" ]]; then
  if [[ -f "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE" ]]; then
    print_info ".env.local already exists — leaving it untouched"
  else
    cp "$ENV_LOCAL_EXAMPLE" "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE"
    print_success "Created .env.local from .env.local.example (edit later for OAuth/IdP credentials)"
  fi
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: ensure required PII keys are present in .env
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# get_value KEY  — print the current value (after the '=') or empty.
get_value() {
  local key="$1"
  # match either KEY=value or KEY= (blank). Strip trailing whitespace/CR.
  grep -E "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | sed -E "s/^${key}=//; s/[[:space:]]*\$//; s/\r\$//"
}

# set_value KEY VALUE  — replace existing KEY= line, or append if absent.
set_value() {
  local key="$1"
  local value="$2"
  if grep -qE "^${key}=" "$ENV_FILE"; then
    # Use a tmp file to stay portable across BSD/GNU sed.
    awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
      BEGIN { FS=OFS="=" }
      $1 == k { print k "=" v; next }
      { print }
    ' "$ENV_FILE" > "$ENV_FILE.tmp" && mv "$ENV_FILE.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
  else
    # Append with a leading blank line for readability if file doesn't end in one.
    [[ -n "$(tail -c1 "$ENV_FILE")" ]] && echo "" >> "$ENV_FILE"
    echo "${key}=${value}" >> "$ENV_FILE"
  fi
}

# fill_if_blank KEY GENERATOR_CMD  — generate + set only when current value is empty.
fill_if_blank() {
  local key="$1"
  local generator="$2"
  local current
  current="$(get_value "$key")"
  if [[ -z "$current" ]]; then
    local generated
    generated="$(eval "$generator")"
    set_value "$key" "$generated"
    print_success "Generated $key (32-byte hex)"
  else
    print_info "$key already set — leaving it"
  fi
}

# fill_default KEY DEFAULT  — set only when current value is empty.
fill_default() {
  local key="$1"
  local default="$2"
  local current
  current="$(get_value "$key")"
  if [[ -z "$current" ]]; then
    set_value "$key" "$default"
    print_success "Set $key=$default"
  else
    print_info "$key already set — leaving it"
  fi
}

# KS-1166: resolve a published host port the way compose does — the SHELL first,
# then .env, then the slot-1 literal. Before this the order was .env → shell →
# literal (KS-731, QA F-731-03), which is right for a clone whose .env has been
# edited for its slot but wrong for the path this script exists to serve: on a
# fresh clone .env was copied from .env.example a moment ago, .env.example ships
# POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT=6432 / REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT=6379, so the .env branch
# always answered and the slot port stack_env.sh had exported into the shell was
# never read. Measured on slots 2 and 3 (2026-09-14): the shell held each slot's
# own port, the generated DATABASE_URL still ended `@localhost:6432/…` — host
# tooling on every slot talked to slot 1's Postgres, F-731-03 in its mirror
# image. Shell-first is also what
# docker-compose.yml does with `${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT:-6432}` (KS-785), so
# the URL and the port compose actually publishes now come from the same answer.
# The .env branch stays second so the F-731-03 case (shell unset, .env edited)
# still resolves to the edited value.
resolve_port() {   # resolve_port KEY SLOT1_LITERAL
  local key="$1" literal="$2" v
  v="${!key:-}"                              # shell: stack_env.sh or an operator export
  [[ -z "$v" ]] && v="$(get_value "$key")"   # .env: F-731-03 — shell unset, .env edited
  [[ -z "$v" ]] && v="$literal"              # slot 1
  printf '%s' "$v"
}

# KS-1166: when a slot is NAMED, derive its ports in the one place that derives
# them (CLAUDE.md: every slot value is calculated from slot 1 in stack_env.sh —
# no port arithmetic here). start-secuura.sh sources stack_env.sh before calling
# this script, but `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 bash scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` run by
# hand did not, and silently produced slot 1's URLs. Guarded: with no slot named,
# stack_env.sh would default to slot 1 and export 6432 over an edited .env,
# re-opening F-731-03. A malformed slot makes stack_env.sh exit 2, which ends
# this script — the loud failure is the point.
# LOCAL HOST ONLY (CLAUDE.md MUST, 2026-09-14): stack slots exist for a build on
# a developer's own machine and nothing else. The VM demo, the Container Apps
# template and CI run unslotted — they never name a slot, so this branch never
# fires there and, with no port exported, resolve_port answers .env → literal
# exactly as before KS-1166. Deploying with a slot in the environment is a defect.
if [[ -n "${SECUURA_STACK_SLOT:-}${STACK_SLOT:-}" ]]; then
  PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-$(cd "$DEV_DIR/../.." && pwd)}"
  # shellcheck source=stack_env.sh
  source "$SCRIPT_DIR/stack_env.sh"
  print_info "Stack slot ${SECUURA_STACK_SLOT} named — ports from stack_env.sh (Postgres ${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT}, Redis ${REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT})"
fi

# KS-731: POSTGRES_PASSWORD and REDIS_PASSWORD were static literals in the
# example files, identical on every slot, worktree, clone and machine — so any
# local slot could read, write and DROP any other slot's Postgres AS SUPERUSER,
# and read/write its entire Redis keyspace. Peter measured it live across four
# concurrent slots (#765): all 12 ordered slot pairs connected to each other's
# database, and slot 1 enumerated slot 2's whole 17-key Redis.
#
# The port mapping is NOT the defect and is not touched — a service is reachable
# cross-slot if and only if it publishes a host port, which 6 of 33 do by design.
# What made reachability into capability was one shared password. Generated per
# clone here, exactly as the PII keys and the RS256 keypair already are, a
# cross-slot connection still reaches the port and fails AUTH.
#
# Generated as ONE unit with the URLs that embed them. `DATABASE_URL` and
# `REDIS_URL` carry the password literally, so filling the password alone would
# leave a .env whose two halves disagree — a stack that authenticates from
# compose and fails from host tooling, which reads as a broken database rather
# than a stale URL. The JWT block below takes the same shape for the same reason.
#
# fill_if_blank semantics matter for adoption: an EXISTING clone already has
# these set, so nothing changes for it and no stack breaks. Only a fresh clone
# gets generated credentials. Moving an existing clone off the shared password
# needs a `--remove-volumes` teardown per slot, because Postgres honours
# POSTGRES_PASSWORD only on first init — see systemTest/CLAUDE.md.
print_info "Checking per-clone datastore credentials in .env (KS-731)..."
if [[ -z "$(get_value POSTGRES_PASSWORD)" ]]; then
  pg_pw="$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
  pg_user="$(get_value POSTGRES_USER)"; [[ -z "$pg_user" ]] && pg_user="secuura"
  pg_db="$(get_value POSTGRES_DB)";     [[ -z "$pg_db" ]] && pg_db="secuura"
  # KS-1166: shell → .env → slot-1 literal; see resolve_port for why the KS-731
  # F-731-03 order (.env first) wrote slot 1's port on every fresh clone.
  pg_port="$(resolve_port POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT 6432)"
  set_value "POSTGRES_PASSWORD" "$pg_pw"
  set_value "DATABASE_URL" "postgresql://${pg_user}:${pg_pw}@localhost:${pg_port}/${pg_db}"
  print_success "Generated POSTGRES_PASSWORD and rebuilt DATABASE_URL to match"
else
  print_info "POSTGRES_PASSWORD already set — leaving it, and DATABASE_URL untouched"
fi

if [[ -z "$(get_value REDIS_PASSWORD)" ]]; then
  redis_pw="$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
  # KS-1166: same resolution as DATABASE_URL above.
  redis_port="$(resolve_port REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT 6379)"
  set_value "REDIS_PASSWORD" "$redis_pw"
  set_value "REDIS_URL" "redis://:${redis_pw}@localhost:${redis_port}"
  print_success "Generated REDIS_PASSWORD and rebuilt REDIS_URL to match"
else
  print_info "REDIS_PASSWORD already set — leaving it, and REDIS_URL untouched"
fi

print_info "Checking PII encryption keys in .env..."
fill_if_blank "PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY"   "openssl rand -hex 32"
fill_default  "PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION" "1"
fill_if_blank "PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY"  "openssl rand -hex 32"

# KS-641 (#737 review): demo-service refuses to start without both of these, and
# compose no longer supplies a default for either — so without this the stack
# comes up with demo-service down. It mints Platform Admin tokens with no caller
# credential, hence a generated key rather than a literal.
print_info "Checking demo-service opt-in in .env..."
fill_default  "DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED" "true"
fill_if_blank "DEMO_SERVICE_KEY"     "openssl rand -hex 32"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RS256 JWT signing keypair (KS-167/184 — JWT is RS256-only; auth is the sole
# signer and holds the private key, verifiers hold the public key). The triple
# is correlated, so generate all three atomically when the private key is blank
# (fill_if_blank can't express a correlated keypair). Without this, auth fails
# fast at startup (no HS256 fallback since KS-184).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
print_info "Checking RS256 JWT signing keypair in .env..."
if [[ -z "$(get_value JWT_PRIVATE_KEY)" ]]; then
  jwt_priv_pem="$(openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 2>/dev/null)"
  jwt_pub_pem="$(printf '%s' "$jwt_priv_pem" | openssl pkey -pubout 2>/dev/null)"
  set_value "JWT_PRIVATE_KEY" "$(printf '%s' "$jwt_priv_pem" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
  set_value "JWT_PUBLIC_KEY"  "$(printf '%s' "$jwt_pub_pem"  | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
  set_value "JWT_KEY_ID"      "local-$(openssl rand -hex 4)"
  print_success "Generated RS256 JWT signing keypair (JWT_PRIVATE_KEY / JWT_PUBLIC_KEY / JWT_KEY_ID)"
else
  print_info "JWT_PRIVATE_KEY already set — leaving the keypair"
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KYC callback credential in .env.local (KS-488-C hardening, back-fill)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The kyc container reads env_file .env.local ONLY — a value in .env never
# reaches it. Fresh setups get KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY from .env.local.example,
# but a pre-existing .env.local created before the variable was added stays
# without it forever, so the service falls back to its known default and the
# KS-488-C callback-auth guard (tests/test_kyc_callback_auth.py) fails.
# Back-fill it here, preferring the .env value when one exists (keeps the two
# files agreeing on machines that set it in .env first).
if [[ -f "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE" ]]; then
  kyc_local="$(grep -E "^KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY=" "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE" 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | sed -E "s/^KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY=//; s/[[:space:]]*\$//; s/\r\$//")"
  if [[ -z "$kyc_local" ]]; then
    kyc_value="$(get_value KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY)"
    [[ -z "$kyc_value" ]] && kyc_value="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
    if grep -qE "^KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY=" "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE"; then
      awk -v v="$kyc_value" 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="="} $1=="KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY"{print $1 "=" v; next} {print}' \
        "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE" > "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE.tmp" && mv "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE.tmp" "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE"
    else
      [[ -n "$(tail -c1 "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE")" ]] && echo "" >> "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE"
      echo "KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY=${kyc_value}" >> "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE"
    fi
    print_success "Back-filled KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY into .env.local (kyc reads only .env.local)"
  else
    print_info "KYC_CALLBACK_API_KEY already set in .env.local — leaving it"
  fi
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Git hooks activation (KS-469 cause 3 / KS-380)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The pre-push preflight gate lives in .githooks/ but needs a per-clone
# `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` opt-in — which stayed unset on real
# clones, so the gate never fired. Developers all run this script (the RS256
# keypair made it mandatory), so activate here: idempotent, relative path,
# repo-local config. NOTE this switches the pre-push preflight ON for clones
# where it never ran — that is the point (decision on KS-469).
repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$repo_root" && -d "$repo_root/.githooks" ]]; then
  current_hooks="$(git -C "$repo_root" config core.hooksPath || true)"
  if [[ "$current_hooks" != ".githooks" ]]; then
    git -C "$repo_root" config core.hooksPath .githooks
    print_success "Activated repo githooks (core.hooksPath=.githooks — pre-push preflight gate, KS-380)"
  else
    print_info "Repo githooks already active (core.hooksPath=.githooks)"
  fi
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Done
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
print_header "BOOTSTRAP COMPLETE"
print_info "Files: $ENV_FILE $( [[ -f "$ENV_LOCAL_FILE" ]] && echo "and $ENV_LOCAL_FILE" )"
print_info "Both files are gitignored. Don't commit them."
echo ""
print_info "Next: docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d"
echo ""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for scripts/bootstrap-env.sh — DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL carry the SLOT's
# host ports, not slot 1's (KS-1166)
# =============================================================================
# bootstrap-env.sh generates DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL for a fresh clone. It
# resolved the host port as .env → shell → slot-1 literal (KS-731, QA F-731-03).
# On a fresh clone .env is the unedited .env.example, which ships
# POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT=6432 / REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT=6379 — so the .env branch
# always answered and the slot port stack_env.sh exported into the shell was
# never read. Measured on slots 2 and 3 on 2026-09-14: shell held each slot's port,
# generated DATABASE_URL `@localhost:6432/…`. Containers never noticed (they
# reach Postgres by compose name); host tooling reading the URL talked to
# slot 1 — F-731-03 in its mirror image.
#
# These cases drive the REAL script in a scratch tree (its own copy of
# bootstrap-env.sh, stack_env.sh and .env.example, so it locates everything
# from its own path and touches no real .env) and read back ONLY the port
# digits of the generated URLs — never the line, which carries the generated
# password. Expectations are DERIVED from the slot-1 bases as base + 100*(N-1),
# never typed per slot (CLAUDE.md, 2026-09-14).
#
# Red on the script as it stood before KS-1166, green after:
#   git show origin/develop:Blockchain/Dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh > /tmp/old-bootstrap.sh
#   BOOTSTRAP_SH=/tmp/old-bootstrap.sh bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
DEV_DIR="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$DEV_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
BOOTSTRAP="${BOOTSTRAP_SH:-$HERE/../bootstrap-env.sh}"
ENV_SH="$HERE/../stack_env.sh"
ENV_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"
[[ -f "$BOOTSTRAP" ]]   || { echo "FATAL: bootstrap-env.sh not found at $BOOTSTRAP" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$ENV_SH" ]]      || { echo "FATAL: stack_env.sh not found at $ENV_SH" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$ENV_EXAMPLE" ]] || { echo "FATAL: .env.example not found at $ENV_EXAMPLE" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: openssl required (bootstrap-env.sh needs it)" >&2; exit 2; }
PASS=0
FAIL=0

# Slot-1 bases. Every per-slot expectation is base + 100*(N-1) — the same
# derivation stack_env.sh performs — so this file cannot encode a slot number
# stack_env.sh does not, and a wrong literal cannot pass against another.
readonly BASE_PG=6432 BASE_REDIS=6379
pg_port()    { echo $(( BASE_PG    + 100 * ($1 - 1) )); }
redis_port() { echo $(( BASE_REDIS + 100 * ($1 - 1) )); }

# The .env.example the script copies must still ship the slot-1 literals — that
# is the premise of the defect (a fresh .env that already "answers" 6432). If the
# template changes shape, these cases would pass for the wrong reason.
tmpl_pg="$(grep -E '^POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT=' "$ENV_EXAMPLE" | head -n1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '[:space:]')"
tmpl_redis="$(grep -E '^REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT=' "$ENV_EXAMPLE" | head -n1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '[:space:]')"
[[ "$tmpl_pg" == "$BASE_PG" && "$tmpl_redis" == "$BASE_REDIS" ]] || {
  echo "FATAL: .env.example no longer ships POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT=$BASE_PG / REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT=$BASE_REDIS (got '$tmpl_pg' / '$tmpl_redis') — premise of this suite changed" >&2
  exit 2
}

# KS-786 / KS-1016: strip every variable stack_env.sh honours with `${VAR:-…}`
# before running a case, measured under `env -i` exactly as stack_env.test.sh
# does. Without it, a shell that has sourced systemTest/slot-target.sh for
# slot 3 would hand the "no slot named" cases slot 3's ports and they would pass
# or fail for the wrong reason.
measured_stack_vars() {
  env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" PROJECT_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT" SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2 \
    bash -c "source '$ENV_SH' >/dev/null 2>&1; set -o posix; set" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=' | cut -d= -f1 \
    | grep -vE '^(HOME|PATH|PWD|SHLVL|OLDPWD|PROJECT_ROOT|IFS|PS[1-4]|BASH[A-Z_]*|OPTERR|OPTIND|PPID|UID|EUID|HOSTNAME|HOSTTYPE|MACHTYPE|OSTYPE|TERM|LINENO|RANDOM|SECONDS|COLUMNS|LINES|GROUPS|DIRSTACK|FUNCNAME|HISTCMD|SHELLOPTS|POSIXLY_CORRECT|_)$'
}
STACK_VARS=(SECUURA_STACK_SLOT STACK_SLOT STACK_PREFIX COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME STACK_BRANCH PROJECT_ROOT)
while IFS= read -r v; do STACK_VARS+=("$v"); done < <(measured_stack_vars)
[[ ${#STACK_VARS[@]} -gt 10 ]] || { echo "FATAL: measured only ${#STACK_VARS[@]} stack variables — the strip set is not being measured" >&2; exit 2; }
STRIP=(); for v in "${STACK_VARS[@]}"; do STRIP+=(-u "$v"); done

# --- scratch tree ------------------------------------------------------------
# bootstrap-env.sh resolves DEV_DIR from its own location and reads
# scripts/stack_env.sh beside itself, so a scratch Blockchain/Dev with those
# two scripts and the real .env.example is a complete fresh clone as far as the
# script can tell. mktemp lives outside any git checkout, so the githooks step
# (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) finds nothing and is a no-op.
SCRATCH_ROOT="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1166.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$SCRATCH_ROOT"' EXIT
new_scratch() {   # new_scratch NAME → echoes the scratch Blockchain/Dev path
  local dev="$SCRATCH_ROOT/$1/Blockchain/Dev"
  mkdir -p "$dev/scripts"
  cp "$BOOTSTRAP" "$dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh"
  cp "$ENV_SH"    "$dev/scripts/stack_env.sh"
  cp "$ENV_EXAMPLE" "$dev/.env.example"
  echo "$dev"
}

# run_bootstrap DEV [VAR=value ...] — run the script with a scrubbed environment
# plus the given assignments; stdout/stderr go to $dev/bootstrap.log; echoes rc.
run_bootstrap() {
  local dev="$1"; shift
  env "${STRIP[@]}" HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" "$@" \
    bash "$dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh" >"$dev/bootstrap.log" 2>&1
  echo $?
}

# Port digits ONLY. The URL lines carry a generated password — never print them.
url_pg_port()    { sed -nE 's#^DATABASE_URL=.*@localhost:([0-9]+)/.*$#\1#p' "$1/.env" | head -n1; }
url_redis_port() { sed -nE 's#^REDIS_URL=.*@localhost:([0-9]+)[[:space:]]*$#\1#p' "$1/.env" | head -n1; }

expect() {
  local desc="$1" want="$2" got="$3"
  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$desc"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n       want "%s", got "%s"\n' "$desc" "$want" "$got"
  fi
}

# --- 1. UNSLOTTED: nothing named, nothing exported → historic ports, unchanged --
# This is every build that is NOT on a developer's local host — the VM demo, the
# Container Apps template, CI, a teammate's plain clone (CLAUDE.md MUST,
# 2026-09-14: slots are a local-host mechanism only). KS-1166 must change
# nothing here: no slot named, no port exported → .env → slot-1 literal.
dev="$(new_scratch unslotted)"
expect "unslotted (VM/CI shape): bootstrap exits 0"           "0" "$(run_bootstrap "$dev")"
expect "unslotted (VM/CI shape): DATABASE_URL port unchanged" "$(pg_port 1)"    "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
expect "unslotted (VM/CI shape): REDIS_URL port unchanged"    "$(redis_port 1)" "$(url_redis_port "$dev")"
expect "unslotted (VM/CI shape): stack_env.sh was NOT consulted" "no" \
  "$(grep -q 'ports from stack_env.sh' "$dev/bootstrap.log" && echo yes || echo no)"

# --- 2. SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N alone → slot N's ports, every slot 1..4 -----------
# This is the by-hand LOCAL shape: `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N bash scripts/bootstrap-env.sh`
# with stack_env.sh NOT sourced by the caller. Slot 1 named explicitly must still
# give the historic ports; red on develop for every N > 1.
for n in 1 2 3 4; do
  dev="$(new_scratch "slot$n")"
  expect "slot $n (SECUURA_STACK_SLOT only): bootstrap exits 0" "0" "$(run_bootstrap "$dev" SECUURA_STACK_SLOT="$n")"
  expect "slot $n (SECUURA_STACK_SLOT only): DATABASE_URL port = $BASE_PG + 100*($n-1)"    "$(pg_port "$n")"    "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
  expect "slot $n (SECUURA_STACK_SLOT only): REDIS_URL port = $BASE_REDIS + 100*($n-1)"   "$(redis_port "$n")" "$(url_redis_port "$dev")"
done

# --- 3. STACK_SLOT alias (shared with platform-s, KS-666 / PS-622), slots 1..4 --
for n in 1 2 3 4; do
  dev="$(new_scratch "alias$n")"
  expect "STACK_SLOT=$n alias: bootstrap exits 0"    "0" "$(run_bootstrap "$dev" STACK_SLOT="$n")"
  expect "STACK_SLOT=$n alias: DATABASE_URL port"    "$(pg_port "$n")"    "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
  expect "STACK_SLOT=$n alias: REDIS_URL port"       "$(redis_port "$n")" "$(url_redis_port "$dev")"
done

# --- 4. shell exports the ports, no slot named (what start-secuura.sh hands over)
# start-secuura.sh sources stack_env.sh (exports POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT /
# REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT) and then runs bootstrap as a child process. The shell
# must beat the template's 6432/6379 — the exact miss measured on slots 2/3.
# Red on develop for every N > 1; slot 1 is the no-op control.
for n in 1 2 3 4; do
  dev="$(new_scratch "shellports$n")"
  expect "shell ports for slot $n, no slot named: bootstrap exits 0" "0" \
    "$(run_bootstrap "$dev" POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT="$(pg_port "$n")" REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT="$(redis_port "$n")")"
  expect "shell ports for slot $n, no slot named: DATABASE_URL takes the shell's port over the template's" "$(pg_port "$n")"    "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
  expect "shell ports for slot $n, no slot named: REDIS_URL takes the shell's port over the template's"    "$(redis_port "$n")" "$(url_redis_port "$dev")"
done

# --- 5. F-731-03 must stay closed: shell unset, .env edited for its slot -------
# An existing clone whose .env carries its slot's ports but whose passwords are
# still blank (the KS-731 adoption path). No slot named, nothing exported:
# the edited .env value must win over the slot-1 literal.
dev="$(new_scratch f73103)"
sed -E "s/^POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT=.*/POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT=$(pg_port 2)/; s/^REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT=.*/REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT=$(redis_port 2)/; s/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=/; s/^REDIS_PASSWORD=.*/REDIS_PASSWORD=/" \
  "$dev/.env.example" > "$dev/.env"
expect "F-731-03: bootstrap exits 0"                              "0" "$(run_bootstrap "$dev")"
expect "F-731-03: edited .env port wins when the shell is unset"  "$(pg_port 2)"    "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
expect "F-731-03: edited .env Redis port wins when shell is unset" "$(redis_port 2)" "$(url_redis_port "$dev")"

# --- 6. existing clone with credentials already set → URLs untouched under any slot
# fill-if-blank semantics: a populated POSTGRES_PASSWORD means DATABASE_URL is
# left alone even when a different slot is named. A sentinel port that is not
# any slot's proves nothing rewrote the line.
# Edited IN PLACE, not appended: get_value reads the FIRST `KEY=` line, so an
# appended value after the template's blank one would read as blank.
dev="$(new_scratch existing)"
sentinel=59999
sed -E "s/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=already-set-not-a-real-secret/; s/^REDIS_PASSWORD=.*/REDIS_PASSWORD=already-set-not-a-real-secret/; s#^DATABASE_URL=.*#DATABASE_URL=postgresql://secuura:already-set-not-a-real-secret@localhost:${sentinel}/secuura#; s#^REDIS_URL=.*#REDIS_URL=redis://:already-set-not-a-real-secret@localhost:${sentinel}#" \
  "$dev/.env.example" > "$dev/.env"
expect "existing clone: fixture has the sentinel port before the run" "$sentinel" "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
expect "existing clone: bootstrap exits 0 under SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3" "0" "$(run_bootstrap "$dev" SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3)"
expect "existing clone: DATABASE_URL untouched"                       "$sentinel" "$(url_pg_port "$dev")"
expect "existing clone: REDIS_URL untouched"                          "$sentinel" "$(url_redis_port "$dev")"
expect "existing clone: exactly one DATABASE_URL line"                "1" "$(grep -cE '^DATABASE_URL=' "$dev/.env")"

# --- 7. malformed slot → loud failure, no URL generated ------------------------
dev="$(new_scratch badslot)"
rc="$(run_bootstrap "$dev" SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=abc)"
expect "bad slot: bootstrap exits non-zero"               "no" "$([[ "$rc" == "0" ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
expect "bad slot: names the slot in its output"           "yes" "$(grep -q "stack slot must be a positive integer" "$dev/bootstrap.log" && echo yes || echo no)"
expect "bad slot: no DATABASE_URL was generated"          ""  "$(url_pg_port "$dev" 2>/dev/null)"

# --- summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "bootstrap_env_slot_ports: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]
